lines.en: Ignoring how depressing and likely true that last line is, the camera fades to black as I turn my head to look behind me, searching for lighter footsteps to cut the darkness in two.
I find them and follow them home despite knowing the way there. It feels more real this way even when I know it’s not.
When I fall asleep tonight, I wonder what will happen.
If there will be a dream within this dream that defies all odds and bequeaths unto me one more layer of undeserved happiness to mesh with that which I unknowingly claimed over the last fifteen years.
If I do dream, I think it will be easier to make myself believe any of this life that feels far too good to be true, yet far too scary to not be.
There’s a light blue key strangled by braided metal in my pocket that I introduce to the lock of our door before pulling it open and finding out that home was never nowhere at all.
It was just a decade and a half away.
: Okay! Now that I have been fed, I will leave you two to get back to whatever weird adult stuff you were doing before I came home! Just hopefully with less fainting this time.
: Are you going to bed already, Himawari? Isn’t it a little early?
: Bed? Oh, no. I just have a lot of homework to do. I’ll come say goodnight before I go to sleep.
: Why do your homework at all if you’re planning on dropping out and letting me home-school you?
: Akira...
: What? She’s old enough to make her own decisions.
: It’s that exact sentiment that ultimately spawned me in the first place! Great thinking as always, Dad! Or shall I say — Sensei?
: Please don’t.
: Hima-chan, go do your homework. And never call your father “Sensei” again.
: I don’t get it.
: But okay! Love you! Want me to start the bath? Or make tea or something?
: Don’t worry about us. Just...go to your room and I’ll make some tea for all of us. Want me to bring it you?
: Yes, please! This brain is not wider than the sky, but I will continue to work hard so that, one day, it might be!
: Oh! I want houjicha! And the creampuff I brought back from Beard Papa’s last night! It should still be good, I think! I hope!
: Hah...
: Stressed already, darling? Did taking care of Ami for all those years not properly prepare you for legitimate fatherhood?
: No, Ayane. That’s been like the main conflict in my character arc over the last couple years back in reality. Pay more attention.
: It was a joke, Akira. I know you do or...did all you could for her, I guess.
: Plus, you were like a dad to me too at first. Until you...impregnated me and dragged me all the way to Aomori.
: Which I am obviously thankful for since it seems to have given us the chance to start over.
: So I guess what I’m saying is...there’s a pretty clear difference so far between the way you see Hima-chan and the way you saw your first daughter.
: Or daughters depending on whether or not I count. Which I probably shouldn’t because, again, you bred me.
: If you’re done explaining your “joke” now, I would like to ask something. Assuming I am allowed, that is.
: Of course, dearest husband. You are always free to speak your mind in our humble abode. I just hope it’s something happy this time.
: Why do you think I left her behind?
: Who, Ami? I’m...not really sure. We teleported here together, remember?
: Yeah, just...I can’t really fathom how you getting pregnant would have spiraled into me abandoning her. And you apparently don’t have her number either, so-
: Please don’t tell me you’re going to get hung up on her while we’re here. I’d like to keep all talks of incest out of this house, thank you very much.
: I’m not going to get hung up. I’m just...
: A lot of time has apparently gone by since we left Kumon-mi. Surely I’m not the only one who’s curious about how the others ended up, right?
: I’m curious too, obviously. I just know better than to go chasing after what we chose to leave behind when what we found is so much better.
: Yeah...I guess you’re right. I’ll try not to bring it up anymore.
: You can bring it up, Akira. Just-
: I’m going to head to the bedroom and try to unwind if that’s okay. With the exception of fainting earlier, I haven’t really slept since before I met Horseface Taki.
: Well...I’m sure it didn’t help that I slapped you out of the only bit of sleep you have gotten, so...sure. Head off to bed and I’ll meet up with you in a few minutes. Do you want tea?
: No thanks, Ayane.
: A bath, perhaps?
: Or maybe...me?
: Or maybe...me?
: I heard you the first time.
: Then why didn’t you say anything? I offer you my voluptuous adult body and you remain silent? You were so excited earlier.
: I still am. I just...feel weird about it while she’s home.
: Akira...that’s adorable. This is the happiest I’ve ever been to have my advances refused.
: It is also the only time I have ever had my advances refused.
: I figured I’d be more offended by that if it ever happened. But instead, I’m just proud to see how far you’ve come.
: Talk to her please. About...stuff. Just to see what she knows.
: Yeah, yeah. You want to bring back more than just misery and blah, blah, blah. Just go to the bedroom and I’ll meet up with you in a few. Okay?
: ...Okay.
: And Ayane-
: What now? I know I said you’re always free to speak your mind, but-
: I just wanted to say I love you again.
: That’s all. I- mmmnffff???
: Mmmmnncchu~
: You’re so cute now. I can’t believe you’re like 46.
: Me neither, to be honest. I saw myself in the mirror at the sushi restaurant and I really do look exactly the same.
: Then, let’s hope that luck translates to me from now on as well! Aging is scary!
: Hima-chan? Can I come in?
: You don’t have to ask, Mom. I’ve told you a million times.
: Really? But you should be flooded by hormones at your age and-
: Can it. Whatever you’re about to say, I definitely don’t want to hear. Now, bring me my cream puff.
: You can have your cream puff in a minute. There’s actually something I want to talk to you about, if that’s okay.
: Something serious? Or something fun? Which Himawari should I be right now?
: It’s funny you should ask since that’s...kind of what I wanted to talk to you about.
: You want to talk to me about me not knowing what you want to talk to me about?
: No. What? I want to talk to you about the potentiality of there actually being two Himawaris.
: Oh, okay. That makes way more sense.
: Does it?
: Absolutely not. Do you have a secret drinking problem, Mom? Are you using?
: No, I am not using. And I definitely don’t have a drinking problem. That would reflect poorly upon me as the nutritionist that I am. I just...
: Listen — I know this is probably going to sound crazy. But there’s a reason your father and I were acting a little...strange when you came home today.
: Again, whatever you’re about to say, I definitely don’t want to hear. What you and Dad do when I’m not home is between you guys. I have nothing to do with it.
: It’s not like that, Himawari. We were just...
: We were taking a nap. And we both had a really strange dream. The same dream. And you were in it.
: A dream?
: He and I were younger...and back in the town we grew up in. You know, the one we won’t let you visit.
: Yeah. Rub it in, why don’t you?
: For some reason, everyone else in the dream disappeared. All of our friends...family...they were all just gone. And it was only your dad and me until you showed up.
: But neither one of us recognized you. Or...I guess I technically recognized you. But I didn’t know who you were.
: And you and I were about the same age in the dream, so of course I wasn’t going to assume you were my daughter.
: But anyway, you showed up, and you basically told us that we were going to die if we didn’t do exactly as you said.
: We were a little hesitant at first, but...not having any other options, we decided to stake everything on you.
: So you opened up a magical door and told us we’d be safe as long as we walked through it. That you’d come and get us once the apocalypse ended.
: So we did. And all of a sudden, we were here.
: Crazy dream, right?
: I don’t think it’s crazy, Mom. I think it’s sweet. And pretty accurate too since I’d definitely find a way to spare you guys from the apocalypse if one were to ever happen.
: I guess that sort of explains that whole “traveled through time” thing you said about me earlier too. That was super weird without context, not gonna lie.
: Hima-chan, do you know anything about the world resetting? Or interdimensional travel or magical doors or anything like that? At all?
: No more than the next girl. Was your dream really that believable?
: Believable would be an understatement. But I will tell you that it feels more like a nightmare in retrospect. Especially after seeing all I have here.
: Is that really all you wanted to talk to me about? Just...to confirm I’m not a secret alien version of your daughter who swapped places with the real one or something?
: I told you it was going to sound crazy.
: Yeah, well you sure didn’t disappoint.
: This is the kind of stuff I’d expect from Dad, though. Not you, Mom. Is he the one who put you up to this?
: I’d call it a...joint decision, if anything. He is worried, though.
: He’s not used to being this happy. So any opportunity he gets to believe the rug is about to be pulled out from underneath his feet, he takes it. No questions asked.
: He’s gonna be okay, right? Because I tried to keep it together, but I got pretty freaked out when he fainted earlier and-
: He’ll be fine...I think your cuteness just sent him into shock for a little while.
: Can I...ask you something too, Mom? Something demonstrably less crazy but also a little crazy in the fact that it seems sort of...reckless in a sense?
: Of course you can. Whatever it is, you can ask away.
: I was serious earlier, you know.
: About dropping out...
: And I don’t think I really got that across the way I wanted to.
: Is something going on at school that gave you this idea, Hima-chan? Why do you want to drop out?
: I just...
: I worry about him.
: And with you working and me in school all the time, I...
: I just don’t want him to feel lonely.
: Plus, it’s not like I’m ever really learning anything in school to begin with.
: Like, even my AP classes are laughably easy. So it’s like, what am I even doing there? Wouldn’t I be better off here instead? With a custom-made curriculum?
: You’re really serious about this?
: I am. And I know I’m young. But when you were my age, you-
: You don’t need to remind me what I did when I was your age.
: Just...please don’t follow in my footsteps. Your father doesn’t even like it when boys look at you. The last thing he needs is worrying about you getting pregnant.
: What a coincidence! That’s the last thing I need as well. And one more reason why it would be beneficial to homeschool me as no boys would even get to look at me. We all win.
: Hima-chan...would that really make you happy, though? Or is all of this for his-
: This is where I want to be, Mom.
: Trust me.
: Well...
: Trusting you hasn’t let me down yet, so...
: Let me talk to your father and we can figure out where to go from there.
: Really?! You’ll consider it?!
: We’ll consider it. No promises, though. Because I have seen your father teach firsthand and, bless his heart, but he is the worst teacher in the entire world.
: Don’t worry! I’ll cancel that out as the best student! And after that, we- wait, where’s my tea?
: Oh, I haven’t made it yet. I got distracted by our bonding.
: Mom! I would have just made it on my own if I knew you were going to forget!
: Well, Akira, I think it’s safe to say that our daughter is not a time-traveler.
: Or at least...isn’t one yet? I’ve never really understood how any of that stuff works, to be honest.
: You don’t think she was just lying to you?
: Frankly, I’m not yet convinced she knows how to lie. Every single interaction I have had with her since we woke up here has only made me fall deeper in love with her.
: It’s almost like she’s too good to be true...isn’t it?
: Do you know what she just told me, Akira? Do you know what her reason for wanting to drop out of school is?
: Oh, was she serious about that?
: She wants to be here with you because she’s worried you’ll feel lonely without us.
: Turns out I was right about our genes combining to form the actual perfect human being. I completely understand why we stopped at one instead of a whole football team now.
: What did you tell her?
: About being homeschooled? That we’d talk about it. Because you’re the one who would have to teach her. Which would mean that you’re the one responsible for-
: I know exactly what it means. Teaching’s the only job I’ve ever had.
: Right, which is why I’m trying to give you a rundown of it because the way you taught me is not good enough for Himawari. You will need to be better.
: Do you think I can, Ayane?
: I think you can for her. And I know it’s only been a little while, but I can’t imagine you’d ever put her in harm’s way. What sort of impact will it have on you, though?
: It’s been years since you properly taught. In both our world and this new one.
: I don’t know...
: I’m too tired and still a little too shocked to even imagine it right now.
: Well, on a scale of one to ten, how tired would you say that you are?
: Does the answer to this question determine whether or not we’re having sex?
: No. It does determine the position, though. And whether or not I’ll need to tape your mouth shut.
: You’re the loud one. Shouldn’t we be taping your mouth shut if anything?
: If that’s what turns you on, sure.
: Ayane...
: It just...feels weird knowing she’s right down the hall and-
: If you’re worried about her hearing us, she put her headphones on as soon as I left the room. And I told her I’d convey her “goodnight” message to you, so...
: I think it’s safe to say we won’t be interrupted, darling.
: Come on, Akira. We jumped fifteen years into the future. Having sex with me right now only seems fair seeing as we had to skip over whatever happened during our honeymoon, doesn’t it?
: Ayane-
: I will ask you again — on a scale of cowgirl to backwards spider crawl, how fucking tired are you?
